what the bot is, which use cases work today, and how to deploy it without burning trust:

step 1 -> every working use case has one shape: read, check, apply a rule, write a draft. if your task fits, the bot can take it

step 2 -> five checks before handoff: repeatable, cross-system, rule-based, draft-first, cheap to get wrong. fails one? add a gate or wait

step 3 -> start with sales. 36 LinkedIn drafts queued overnight, none sent without review. no team has more agent-ready work

step 4 -> engineering gets bug repro, CI/CD watch and dependency audits. the bot picks up the ticket, hits staging and hands back a repro pack

step 5 -> operations hands over inbox, expenses and travel. the bot logs into portals that have no API, and finance gets 8-12 hours back at month-end

step 6 -> marketing owns 13 of the 56 roles: paid media, content calendars, competitor watch. all overnight, all draft-first

step 7 -> the approval line: every documented use case stops before external action. nothing gets sent, booked or paid without you

step 8 -> roll out over four weeks: watch, review everything, review flags, then a scheduled routine. skip a week and the risk stacks up

step 9 -> the fleet: a Chief of Staff bot on top, specialists below, bots messaging each other. you stop being the middleman

step 10 -> rank tasks by the cost of a mistake. the bot nails 49 in a row, then does something strange on the 50th with full confidence. keep a human at every exit

the result: 56 roles, one playbook. the bot takes the 80% that repeats, you keep the 20% that matters
